content.title: Does FTC Scrutiny Of Instacart’s AI Pricing And Disclosures Change The Bull Case For Maplebear (CART)?
content.summary: Earlier this month, the FTC accused Instacart parent Maplebear of deceptive advertising and inadequate Instacart+ disclosures, ordering the company to pay US$60 million, while separately opening a probe into its use of AI-driven pricing tools after reports of inconsistent prices for similar shoppers. These twin regulatory actions highlight how central Instacart’s AI pricing and marketing practices have become to its business model, and how closely regulators are now watching them. Next,...

content.title: Instacart Ordered to Pay $60 Million to Settle FTC Deceptive-Practices Claim
content.summary: The FTC alleged that the grocery-delivery platform falsely advertised free delivery and 100% satisfaction guarantee, and also didn’t adequately disclose the terms for Instacart+ membership.

content.title: FTC probes Instacart's AI pricing tool, source says; shares drop
content.summary: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission is probing Instacart, two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters, as the retail platform faces criticism over its artificial intelligence-driven pricing tool.  Instacart shares were down about 10% in after-hours trading.  The agency has sent the company a ​civil investigative demand, the sources said.
